name: org.machanism.machai:bindex-core
description: Bindex Core is a Java 17 Maven library for creating, validating, registering, retrieving, and semantically selecting Bindex metadata records. A Bindex record describes a reusable software artifact as a structured bindex.json document containing Maven coordinates, version, authorship, license, classification, supported languages, Clean Architecture layers, integrations, features, setup instructions, dependencies, and practical usage examples. The library supports AI-assisted software assembly by making reusable libraries discoverable through natural-language requirements. It provides MongoDB-backed persistence, Atlas vector search, classification filtering, embedding generation, library recommendation, recursive dependency resolution, and AI-facing function tools for get_bindex, pick_libraries, register_bindex, and register_bindex_json. It also includes schema model classes generated from the Bindex v2 schema, GraphQL-style filtering for reducing returned metadata, Bindex generation prompts, and built-in Ghostwriter acts for Maven project Bindex generation, Java Javadoc extraction, Bindex registration, and project assembly. Bindex Core is useful for AI agents, MCP servers, Ghostwriter CLI, Maven plugin workflows, CI/CD automation, governed dependency discovery, local or remote Bindex repositories, and teams that want libraries to behave like reusable bricks for application assembly.

usageContext: AI agents that recommend reusable libraries from natural-language prompts
MCP servers that expose Bindex function tools to IDEs and assistants
Ghostwriter and Maven plugin workflows that generate bindex.json files
CI/CD pipelines that validate and register reusable artifact metadata
Local or remote MongoDB-backed Bindex repositories
Java applications that need semantic artifact lookup and registration

constructors.description: Creates an AI-facing function tool set that exposes Bindex discovery, retrieval, registration, schema access, and generation-prompt operations to a host runtime such as Ghostwriter or the Machai MCP Server.

examples.description: Instantiate the function tools directly when embedding Bindex capabilities in a Java host. The host is responsible for supplying project directory and configurator values when invoking tool methods.
examples.snippet:
org.machanism.machai.bindex.ai.tools.BindexFunctionTools tools = new org.machanism.machai.bindex.ai.tools.BindexFunctionTools();
// Register this org.machanism.machai.ai.tools.FunctionTools implementation with the host tool runtime.

constructors.description: Creates a MongoDB-backed repository for persisting and retrieving Bindex documents and their embeddings. Connection settings are resolved from BINDEX_REPO_URL, BINDEX_USER, and BINDEX_PASSWORD through the supplied configurator.

examples.description: Create a repository in a try-with-resources block so its MongoDB client is closed automatically after use.

constructors.description: Creates a picker that uses a Bindex repository plus configured GenAI and embedding providers to save descriptors and recommend relevant libraries for natural-language requirements.

examples.description: Create a picker with a repository and request recommendations above a configured score threshold.
examples.snippet:
org.machanism.machai.bindex.core.Picker picker = new org.machanism.machai.bindex.core.Picker(repository, configurator);
java.util.Collection<org.machanism.machai.bindex.core.BindexInfo> matches = picker.pick("Java library for AI tool metadata lookup and registration", 25L, 0.85d, configurator);

features.name: get_bindex
features.signature: public org.machanism.machai.schema.Bindex getBindex(java.lang.String id, java.lang.String query, java.io.File projectDir, org.machanism.macha.core.commons.configurator.Configurator configurator) throws java.io.IOException
features.description: Retrieves Bindex metadata by coordinates or by a direct descriptor URL. The optional GraphQL-style query filters returned fields so AI agents can request only the metadata they need, such as name, version, classification, dependencies, or examples.

examples.description: How to use it from an AI tool call: request a descriptor by Maven-like Bindex ID and reduce the response to fields needed for dependency selection.
examples.snippet:
org.machanism.machai.bindex.ai.tools.BindexFunctionTools tools = new org.machanism.machai.bindex.ai.tools.BindexFunctionTools();
org.machanism.machai.schema.Bindex bindex = tools.getBindex("org.machanism.machai:bindex-core:1.3.2", "{ name version classification { languages domains } }", projectDir, configurator);

features.name: pick_libraries
features.signature: public java.util.Collection<org.machanism.machai.bindex.core.BindexInfo> getRecommendedLibraries(java.lang.String prompt, double score, int vectorSearchLimits, org.machanism.macha.core.commons.configurator.Configurator configurator) throws java.io.IOException
features.description: Recommends libraries based on a natural-language prompt. The picker classifies the request, generates an embedding, searches the MongoDB-backed Bindex repository, filters by classification and minimum relevance score, and returns matching BindexInfo summaries.

examples.description: How to use it in a planning workflow: ask for libraries that satisfy a development need and retrieve up to 25 highly relevant matches.
examples.snippet: java.util.Collection<org.machanism.machai.bindex.core.BindexInfo> recommendations = tools.getRecommendedLibraries("Need Java tools for Bindex metadata registration, semantic search, and MCP tool exposure", 0.85d, 25, configurator);

features.name: register_bindex
features.signature: public java.lang.String registerBindex(java.lang.String path, java.io.File projectDir, org.machanism.macha.core.commons.configurator.Configurator configurator) throws java.io.IOException
features.description: Registers a Bindex descriptor from a project-relative file path or remote URL. This operation reads the descriptor, normalizes it for repository storage, generates embedding data, and saves it so the artifact becomes available for semantic search and recommendation.

examples.description: How to use it after generating bindex.json in a Maven project: register the local descriptor from the project root.
examples.snippet:
java.lang.String recordId = tools.registerBindex("bindex.json", projectDir, configurator);
// The returned value identifies the saved Bindex record.

features.name: register_bindex_json
features.description: Registers a structured Bindex object directly without first reading a file. This is useful for agent workflows that already assembled a schema-compliant descriptor in memory and want to publish it immediately.

examples.description: How to use it from a Java automation pipeline after constructing a Bindex object programmatically.

features.name: MongoDB-backed Bindex repository
features.signature: public java.util.Collection<org.machanism.machai.bindex.core.BindexInfo> find(org.machanism.machai.schema.Classification[] classifications, java.util.List<java.lang.Double> embedding, long vectorSearchLimits, double score, org.machanism.macha.core.commons.configurator.Configurator config)
features.description: Stores complete Bindex JSON descriptors and searches them using vector similarity plus classification metadata. It supports repository lookup, saving, deletion, and direct collection access for advanced aggregation workflows.

examples.description: How to configure local use: start MongoDB Atlas Local, set repository variables, and let Bindex Core connect through its configurator.

features.name: Bindex generation acts
features.description: Provides built-in Ghostwriter acts for building Maven Javadoc, extracting API documentation, reading Markdown documentation, producing an effective POM, generating a schema-compliant bindex.json file, validating it, registering it, selecting libraries, and assembling projects from natural-language requirements.

examples.description: How to use it in a Maven project: run the Bindex Maven-project workflow to generate documentation, create bindex.json, and validate the result before registration.
examples.snippet:
mvn clean install javadoc:javadoc -Dshow=protected -DreportOutputDirectory="target/reports" -DdestDir="apidocs" -DskipTests -q
mvn help:effective-pom -Doutput=target/effective-pom.xml -q
# Then invoke the Ghostwriter act named bindex/java/mvn-project or the top-level bindex act from the configured host.

studs.name: org.machanism.machai.bindex.core.BindexRepository
studs.description: Repository contract for saving Bindex metadata, retrieving descriptors by ID, and finding records by classification, embedding vector, result limits, and relevance score.

examples.description: Use the interface to decouple the picker from the concrete MongoDB implementation.
examples.snippet:
org.machanism.machai.bindex.core.BindexRepository repository = new org.machanism.machai.bindex.core.MongoBindexRepository(configurator);
org.machanism.machai.bindex.core.Picker picker = new org.machanism.machai.bindex.core.Picker(repository, configurator);

examples.title: Install Bindex Core as a Maven dependency
examples.scenario: Use Bindex Core directly from a Java application or service that needs Bindex metadata lookup, registration, or recommendation support.
steps: Add org.machanism.machai:bindex-core to the Maven project dependencies.
Configure repository and GenAI settings in the host application.
Instantiate BindexFunctionTools, MongoBindexRepository, or Picker depending on the workflow.
Call get_bindex, pick_libraries, register_bindex, or register_bindex_json from the host runtime.
examples.description: This is the standard installation path for Java projects. The artifact is published as a Maven JAR and targets Java 17. After installation, configure BINDEX_REPO_URL, BINDEX_USER, BINDEX_PASSWORD, GENAI_USERNAME, GENAI_PASSWORD, gw.model, and embedding.model as required by your environment.

examples.title: Expose Bindex tools through Machai MCP Server
examples.scenario: Publish Bindex function tools so MCP-compatible clients such as Claude Desktop, Cursor, Windsurf, VS Code, JetBrains IDEs, Zed, or Warp can retrieve descriptors, pick libraries, and register Bindex records.
steps: Download machai-mcp-server.jar and bindex-core.jar.
Place both JAR files in the same working directory.
Configure GenAI and embedding model properties.
Start org.machanism.machai.mcp.server.McpServer with bindex-core.jar on the classpath.
Connect an MCP-compatible client to the configured port, for example 45000.
Test with MCP Inspector and verify Bindex tools are listed.
examples.description: This ready-to-use component scenario installs Bindex Core as an MCP server classpath dependency, configures model credentials and model names, and runs a real server process. On Unix-like systems use a colon instead of a semicolon as the classpath separator.

examples.title: Run a local Bindex repository with Dockerized MongoDB Atlas Local
examples.scenario: Use a local repository for development, testing, and validating registration without relying on a shared remote database.
steps: Install Docker Desktop or Docker Engine with Docker Compose support.
Open the src/docker/mongodb directory.
Run docker compose up -d to start MongoDB Atlas Local.
Set BINDEX_REPO_URL to mongodb://localhost:27017/?appName=machanism and set BINDEX_USER=user and BINDEX_PASSWORD=pass.
Optionally connect with MongoDB Compass using mongodb://user:pass@localhost:27017/?authSource=admin&appName=machanism.
Run Bindex registration or recommendation workflows against the local repository.
examples.snippet:
cd src/docker/mongodb
docker compose up -d
set BINDEX_REPO_URL=mongodb://localhost:27017/?appName=machanism
set BINDEX_USER=user
set BINDEX_PASSWORD=pass
examples.description: This example configures the persistence backend required by registration and semantic search. The initialization script creates the machanism database, bindex collection, validation rules, and Atlas Search indexes.

examples.title: Generate and register bindex.json for a Maven project
examples.scenario: Use Bindex Core with Ghostwriter acts to turn Maven project documentation, Javadoc, and effective POM metadata into a schema-compliant Bindex descriptor.
steps: Build Javadoc into target/reports/apidocs.
Generate target/effective-pom.xml with Maven Help Plugin.
Run the bindex/java/extract-javadoc act to extract public API documentation.
Generate bindex.json from Markdown documentation, extracted Javadoc, and the effective POM.
Validate bindex.json against the Bindex v2 schema.
Register bindex.json with register_bindex after reviewing the metadata.
examples.snippet:
mvn clean install javadoc:javadoc -Dshow=protected -DreportOutputDirectory="target/reports" -DdestDir="apidocs" -DskipTests -q
mvn help:effective-pom -Doutput=target/effective-pom.xml -q
# Invoke the Ghostwriter act: bindex/java/mvn-project
# Validate with: get_bindex id=file://bindex.json
examples.description: This scenario produces a discoverable artifact descriptor. The generated examples should show practical installation, configuration, and invocation steps so AI agents understand how to use the library.
